newsitem.title: POLAND: Russian agents work to stop Polish EU, NATO entry.
newsitem.headline: Russian agents work to stop Polish EU, NATO entry.

text.p: Russian secret services are active in trying to create a pro-Russian lobby and block Poland's entry into the European Union and NATO, the Polish security minister said in remarks published on Saturday.
"Russia, through agents of influence among politicians and businessmen, wants to bloc Poland's entry into the EU and NATO," Zbigniew Siemiatkowski told the Rzeczpospolita daily in an interview.
He said agents of influence did not operate by selling information but by creating a climate for making certain decisions thanks to their strategic placement in political and business structures.

"Polish counter-intellingence sees increased contacts of Russian diplomats with politicians from the (ruling) Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and Peasant Party (PSL) as well as from the opposition aimed to create a strong pro-Russian lobby."
Rzeczpospolita quoted Siemiatkowski as saying he expected Russia's secret services to soon stage big provocations aimed at discrediting Poland's drive to join European structures.
"They will show that countries aspiring to NATO have unreliable elites -- corrupt on the one side and loyal to their former bosses on the other," he said.
Last year Poland's Prime Minister Jozef Oleksy from the SLD was forced to resign after allegations he knowingly informed for Moscow.
Oleksy strongly denied the allegations and military prosecutors dropped the case saying there was not enought evidence.

Siemiatkowski said that on the basis of articles published in Moscow's press, secret services may have been behind the replacement of Russia's "soft and realistic" former Foreign Minister Andrei Kozyrev with the hard-line former head of foreign intelligence Yevgeny Primakov.
"He (Primakov) says 'nyet' to Poland's entry into NATO and uses secret services for that purpose," Siemiatkowski said.
He said he soon expected an offensive of Russian diplomacy and secret services through "well tested, old contacts in western media and social organisations" to lobby against NATO expansion.

He said Russain services will influence persons and lobby groups to say: "We need to come to terms with Russia. Russia is too important as a partner to the West to forsake our own interests for some central european countries."
Siemiatkowski told the paper Russia was currently inviting western publishers, congresmen, senators and EU parliament deputies to influence their opinions.
"It has all the characteristics of coordinated actions on the part of Russian secret services," he said.
The paper quoted Siemiatkowski as saying that Russian services were also trying to gain control over strategic sectors of the Polish economy.
"There are attempts to take over strategic sectors of the Polish economy by capital from Russian secret services," Siemiatkowski said.

"Russia wants to have influence over Polish elites and become so strongly rooted in strategic sectors of the economy that it will have to be taken into account when making the decision to join the EU," he said.
